questions.stem: A clerk notes that the flux through a coil changes by 0.080 webers in 0.20 seconds; which statement gives the induced emf?

options.text: The emf is 0.40 volts because the change is divided by the time.
The emf is 0.016 volts because the values are multiplied.
options.misconception: multiplies flux change by time instead of dividing

options.text: The emf is 0.16 volts because the time is doubled.
options.misconception: doubles the time interval in the denominator

options.text: The emf is 0.040 volts because the flux is halved.

questions.explanation: Induced emf equals change in flux divided by change in time, so 0.080 over 0.20 gives 0.40 volts; multiplying or altering values misapplies Faraday's law.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_I
questions.topic: Lenz's law sets the direction of the induced current
questions.learningObjective: Apply Lenz's law to an approaching magnet
questions.stem: A magnet's north pole approaches a coil from the left; which induced current direction is expected?

options.text: The current makes the near face a south pole to attract the magnet.
options.misconception: thinks induced field attracts the magnet

options.text: The current makes the near face a north pole to repel the magnet.
No current flows because the magnet has not touched the coil.
The current flows to cancel the magnet permanently.
options.misconception: assumes induced field removes the magnet

questions.explanation: Lenz's law makes the induced current oppose the change, so the near face becomes a north pole and repels the approaching north pole; attraction or no current violates opposition.
